papers.title_en: WorkFactory: Turning Professional Intents into Executable Work for Scalable Agent Training
papers.authors: Ziyang Zeng, Tingyang Chen, Jia Deng, Qiyao Wang, Shuo Tang, Yike Yang, Tao Ren, Wayne Xin Zhao, Feng Chang, Jujie He, Chuan Hao, Ran Tao, Bryan Dai
papers.evidence: 为智能体训练构建可执行任务的规模化数据管线
papers.tldr: 针对工作型智能体监督训练中专业任务信息缺失或不一致、阻碍教师执行的问题，WorkFactory 从职业意图出发，用信息级规划构建信息支撑图并实例化任务，再通过探针执行诊断支撑失败并修复。作者构建覆盖612种职业的112,686个任务，用教师轨迹微调 Qwen 得到 WorkPilot 系列。三个规模模型在四项基准上均优于基座，35B-A3B 在 GDPval-AA v2.1 的 Elo 从879升至1565，验证了可扩展任务构造与修复机制的价值。
papers.abstract_en: Scaling supervised training for working agents requires diverse professional tasks that yield reliable expert demonstrations. However, missing or inconsistent task information can obstruct teacher execution and weaken the resulting supervision. We propose WorkFactory, a scalable framework for constructing coherent and executable professional tasks. Starting from professional intents, information-level planning builds an information support graph to guide task instantiation, explicitly representing the dependencies and locations of information required for the intended outputs. Probe executions then identify support failures and guide repairs while preserving the intended work. We construct 112,686 tasks spanning 612 occupations and use the collected teacher trajectories to fine-tune Qwen models at 4B, 27B, and 35B-A3B scales, yielding the WorkPilot family. All three models improve over their respective base models across four professional-work benchmarks, with WorkPilot-35B-A3B improving from 879 to 1565 Elo on GDPval-AA v2.1. Scaling analyses reveal model-dependent diminishing returns, with execution length first increasing and then decreasing. Controlled component analyses show that planning and repair reduce probe-diagnosed task environment defects and improve downstream performance. The data and models are available at https://github.com/IQuestLab/WorkFactory.

papers.title_en: MiRL: Error-Targeted Reinforcement Learning for Correcting Terminal Agent Misbehaviors
papers.authors: Runchu Tian, Zaid Khan, Zun Wang, Justin Chih-Yao Chen, Mohit Bansal
papers.evidence: 面向长程多轮终端智能体交互的强化学习
papers.tldr: 终端智能体需在命令行中完成长程任务，但现有错误定向方法只面向单轮任务，失败分析也多用于诊断而非训练。MiRL 先分析策略错误，找出跨环境复现的可泛化错误行为，再从这些错误步骤启动 rollout 做强化学习，仅在通过测试且未重犯该错误时给奖励。在 Qwen3.5-4B 上，8 类错误行为占错误步骤的 52.1%，训练后未见前缀上重犯率降 43%–57%；Terminal-Bench Lite 达 51.8%，超过 TMax-4B 的 47.4%，rollout 用量仅为其 35%。
papers.abstract_en: Error-targeted learning gives a legible way to improve a model: identify specific weaknesses of the model, train the model to fix these weaknesses, and check whether the weaknesses are fixed. We study how to apply error-targeted learning to terminal agents, which solve long-horizon tasks specified in natural language by interacting with a command shell. Existing error-targeted methods are designed for single-turn tasks, and existing analyses of agent failures are used to evaluate and debug agents rather than to train them. We propose Misbehavior-driven RL (MiRL), which first profiles the errors of a policy to find generalizable misbehaviors: kinds of wrong steps that recur across many environments. MiRL then trains the policy with RL, starting rollouts at the steps where these misbehaviors occur and rewarding a rollout only if it passes the tests and avoids the misbehavior. On Qwen3.5-4B, eight misbehaviors account for 52.1% of wrong steps. After training with MiRL, the policy repeats the measured misbehaviors 43% to 57% less often on average on unseen prefixes. MiRL outperforms TMax-4B on Terminal-Bench Lite (51.8% vs. 47.4%) and matches it on Terminal-Bench 2.1 (21.3% vs. 20.6%), while using 35% of its rollouts. These results show that error-targeted learning can be applied to realistic, long-horizon terminal tasks.

papers.title_en: OmniBrain-0: A Unified Agentic Model for Embodied Intelligence
papers.authors: Xiaomi Embodied Intelligence Team, Yuechen Luo, Chong He, Fang Li, Shaoqing Xu, Jingkai Wang, Menglun Su, Jiaxin Liu, Shengyin Jiang, Zhiyi Lai, Long Chen, Longlong Wang, Liang Hu, Haochen Liu, Yuncheng Jiang, Hongwei Xie, Jieming Cui, Hanbing Li, Junjie Huang, Zhixiang Duan, Hexin Zhang, Weixiang Liang, Ying Gong, Yuhan Wang, Yong Pan, Pengna Li, Kangyi Wu, Ken Deng, Kun Ma, Fuxi Wen, Zhi-xin Yang, Hangjun Ye
papers.evidence: 用于训练统一具身智能体的多教师同策略蒸馏
papers.tldr: 通用具身智能需在长时程中协调操作与导航并跟踪进度、从失败恢复，专用策略难以保证任务级可靠性。OmniBrain-0 是轻量统一具身智能体，以共享高层决策模型整合任务理解、规划、进度跟踪与反馈恢复，并通过具身预训练、领域专家蒸馏和多教师在线策略蒸馏逐步整合能力。在 LIBERO-Pro、RoboCasa365、R2R-CE 及真实操作任务上，它兼顾跨域性能并显著降低推理与执行开销。该工作表明可将强教师交互经验高效迁移并巩固到紧凑统一智能体中。
papers.abstract_en: General-purpose embodied intelligence requires robots to coordinate diverse skills over long horizons, track task progress, and recover from failures. Specialist policies alone do not ensure task-level reliability, while powerful multimodal agents rely on costly reasoning and external experience that compact models struggle to reproduce. We introduce OmniBrain-0, a lightweight unified embodied agent that coordinates manipulation and navigation through a shared high-level decision model, integrating task understanding, planning, progress tracking, and feedback-driven recovery. Our progressive training framework combines embodied pretraining, domain-specialized agent distillation, and multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD). It distills powerful teachers' interaction experience into manipulation and navigation experts, then consolidates their decision capabilities into OmniBrain-0. Unification therefore occurs within the learned decision model rather than only at the tool interface. We further introduce Rubric-Guided Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI), a data flywheel in which a Meta-Agent turns execution evidence into refined rubrics, step-level reminders, and verified trajectories for domain-expert updates before their reconsolidation into OmniBrain-0 through MOPD. We evaluate OmniBrain-0 on LIBERO-Pro, LIBERO-Plus, RoboCasa365, RoboTwin 2.0, and R2R-CE Val-Unseen, as well as multiple real-world manipulation tasks. OmniBrain-0 combines strong cross-domain task performance with substantially lower inference and execution overhead than its closed-source teacher, demonstrating efficient transfer and consolidation of embodied capabilities into a compact unified agent.

papers.title_en: CoHARL: Co-Evolving Agent Policies and Executable Harnesses with Reinforcement Learning
papers.authors: Jianwen Chen, Peng Xia, Kaide Zeng, Siwei Han, Zhen-Yu Zhang, Charles Fleming, Xinyu Ye, Huaxiu Yao
papers.evidence: 协同进化智能体策略与工具执行框架的强化学习
papers.tldr: LLM智能体依赖可执行harness完成工具调用与反馈，但固定harness或固定策略都会限制训练效果。CoHARL采用基于种群的强化学习，让共享策略与多个可执行harness共同演化，并用执行轨迹驱动harness代码修订。在SWE-rebench上取得27.6%平均解决率，较仅搜索harness提升6.4个百分点。该工作表明训练中协同适配策略与接口能持续改善智能体经验生成。
papers.abstract_en: Large language model (LLM) agents interact with their environments through executable harnesses that govern tool use and feedback. Optimizing a harness for a fixed policy overlooks how its behavior changes during learning, while training a policy under a fixed harness leaves the interface that generates its training experience unchanged. This motivates adapting the harness throughout policy training. We introduce CoHARL, a population-based reinforcement learning framework that co-evolves a shared policy and a population of executable harnesses. The policy learns from rollouts across the population, and a proposer uses its execution traces to revise harness code during training. CoHARL achieves a 27.6% mean resolved rate on SWE-rebench, improving over harness-only search by 6.4 percentage points. Experiments on SWE-bench Verified and Terminal-Bench 2.0 show gains in software engineering and terminal-based tasks. Under matched training budgets, CoHARL also outperforms searching for a harness once before RL and alternating policy updates with revisions to a single active harness.

papers.title_en: EnvSched: Environment-Aware Scheduling for Rollout-Efficient Agent Reinforcement Learning
papers.authors: Sihan Yang, Weichen Bai, Ruichuan An, Yiming Cheng, Zhiyuan Feng, Tianyi Jiang, Renye Yan, Ning Ding, Yifan Zhang, Renrui Zhang, Yehui Tang, Wentao Zhang
papers.evidence: 面向智能体强化学习的环境级调度
papers.tldr: 智能体强化学习需大量昂贵 rollout，有限预算下如何按环境组织任务实例是关键。EnvSched 用双关系图建模环境—任务对，沿环境内/跨环境边传播历史 rollout 统计，预测任务奖励方差。调度器优先高方差任务并覆盖欠观察环境，配合配额与相似度惩罚提升批次信息量和多样性。在 Qwen3-8B 上，40 步训练即达 BFCL-v3、tau-Bench、ACEBench-Agent 平均 48.81，超过随机选择 120 步的最高分。
papers.abstract_en: As executable environments for language agents scale, generating and verifying their rollouts becomes increasingly expensive. Under finite rollout budgets, this raises an important question: can data management at the environment level make agentic reinforcement learning (RL) more efficient by organizing, evaluating, and scheduling task instances together with the environments that determine their tools, states, transitions, and verification? To address this question, we introduce EnvSched (Environment-aware Scheduling), an online scheduler that learns from rollout history. EnvSched assigns scheduling value through two complementary modeling choices: exploitation prioritizes tasks likely to provide informative reward differences, while coverage spreads each batch across underobserved environments and interaction patterns. EnvSched organizes environment--task pairs as nodes in a dual-relation graph, with within-environment edges capturing task semantics and shared tool, state, and verifier structure, and cross-environment edges capturing abstract execution and reward topology. By propagating historical rollout statistics along both edge types, it predicts within-task reward variance. These predictions guide a scheduler that allocates each batch to tasks with high predicted reward variance and underobserved environments and tasks. Environment quotas and a similarity penalty further limit concentration and redundancy, yielding informative and diverse batches without additional pilot rollouts. In RL on Qwen3-8B, EnvSched achieves an average score of 48.81 across BFCL-v3, tau-Bench, and ACEBench-Agent after 40 training steps, exceeding the highest score attained by random task selection after 120 steps. It also improves downstream performance across model sizes at the same training budget.

papers.title_en: GEPA-Curator: Curated Learning for Self Improving Agents
papers.authors: Zack Yu, Nicholas Lee, Minjae Lee, Lakshya Agarwal, Luca Manolache, Wonjun Kang, Matei Zaharia, Michael W. Mahoney, Kurt Keutzer, Sehoon Kim, Amir Gholami
papers.evidence: 任务整理筛选用于提示优化的智能体经验
papers.tldr: LLM 智能体在多轮任务中常因提示词、执行环境、随机性或评审噪声而失败，现有 GEPA 等反思式优化器直接学习失败轨迹可能引入噪声甚至有害信号。GEPA-Curator 通过任务筛选剔除不可靠学习样本，并检索历史成功轨迹作为优化器上下文。在 GoBrowse、ALFWorld、AppWorld 与 τ-bench 上，使用 Gemini 3.1 Pro 和 Claude Opus 5 评测，平均性能匹配或超过基线，最高较 GEPA 提升 20.7%、较 ACE 提升 21.2%。该工作强调经验筛选对自改进智能体的重要性。
papers.abstract_en: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used in multi-turn agentic workloads that require sustained interaction with complex environments. Existing reflective prompt optimizers such as GEPA learn from failed rollouts, but agentic failures can also come from prompt weaknesses, harness limitations, stochastic execution, or noisy judges. We argue that such failures may not provide useful learning signal, and may even be harmful; and thus it is essential to curate which tasks are provided to the prompt optimizer for better performance. We introduce GEPA-Curator, a framework that augments the prompt optimizer to select which agent experiences should shape prompt optimization. In particular, GEPA-Curator consists of two components: task curation, which filters out tasks that are likely to provide noisy or unreliable learning signals, and prior success retrieval, which selectively retrieves past successful trajectories for a task and provides them as additional context to the prompt optimizer. We evaluate GEPA-Curator on GoBrowse, ALFWorld, AppWorld, and $τ$-bench, using both Gemini 3.1 Pro and Claude Opus 5 as optimizer models. GEPA-Curator matches or exceeds the mean performance of both baselines, with gains of up to 20.7% over GEPA and 21.2% over ACE.

papers.title_en: Where to Learn and How Far to Roll Out: Efficient Adaptive Training for GUI Agents
papers.authors: Yuxiang Chai, Quyu Kong, Panrong Tong, Steven Hoi, Yue Wang
papers.evidence: 多步GUI智能体的自适应强化学习训练
papers.tldr: 轨迹级GRPO训练GUI智能体需反复rollout，任务级奖励监督粗糙且已掌握前缀被重复执行。论文提出两阶段自适应框架：从专家轨迹构建可复用检查点，用动作分歧选pivot；Stage I在pivot做一步RL改进局部决策，Stage II按进度扩展Local、Suffix、Root训练。在MobileGym与CUA-Gym-Hub上较Vanilla GRPO减少56-61%交互并提升表现，表明联合分配状态与rollout范围可提升RL效率。
papers.abstract_en: Trajectory-level GRPO is a common approach for training multi-step GUI agents, but repeatedly rolling out complete trajectories from the task root can be inefficient: task-level rewards provide coarse supervision over which intermediate decisions require improvement, while already-mastered prefixes are repeatedly re-executed before reaching difficult states. We introduce a two-stage adaptive training framework that jointly addresses where to learn and how far to roll out. We first construct reusable intermediate checkpoints from successful expert trajectories and select informative pivots using action disagreement, which measures uncertainty directly from sampled GUI actions. Stage I performs one-step RL at these pivots to improve uncertain local decisions. Stage II then progressively expands policy responsibility through adaptive Local, Suffix, and Root training according to task progress. Recoverable checkpoints enable repeated training from intermediate states without replaying the preceding trajectory. Across MobileGym and CUA-Gym-Hub, our method reduces environment interaction by 56-61% relative to Vanilla GRPO while improving task performance, demonstrating that jointly allocating training across states and rollout ranges can substantially improve GUI-agent RL efficiency.

papers.title_en: From Intent to Improvement: Agentic Dataset Search for Better Model Training
papers.authors: Qiaosheng Chen, Kaijia Huang, Fanqi Zhou, Gong Cheng
papers.evidence: 面向训练约束的智能体数据集搜索
papers.tldr: 在百万级机器学习仓库中找训练数据，仅靠文本相关性不足，查询还包含任务、许可和训练阶段等硬约束，且元数据常缺失。AgenticDS 将查询编译为类型化搜索计划，以确定性算子执行混合检索与有界图扩展，并在接受排序前核验溯源证据。在 HuDS-Bench 上，其 NDCG@10 较最强稠密-稀疏混合检索提升 25.7%，较商业 LLM 智能体提升 18.9%。搜索到训练实验还显示，检索数据在数学、代码和医学任务上取得最佳下游准确率。
papers.abstract_en: Finding training data in million-scale machine learning repositories is a Web search problem where text relevance is not enough. A query couples a semantic training goal with constraints such as task, license, and training stage, and the metadata that would verify them are often missing. Text retrieval ranks dataset cards by similarity but cannot enforce hard constraints or follow the relations that reach a sparsely described dataset. Free-form tool-calling agents are more flexible, but the same model that picks a dataset also declares it a match, and nothing checks that the query's constraints are actually met. Neither approach establishes that the data it returns will improve model training. To address it, we propose AgenticDS, a contract-governed agentic framework in which every language model decision instantiates a typed object before deterministic code consumes it. The framework compiles a query into a typed search plan, executes it through admissible deterministic operators over hybrid retrieval and bounded graph expansion, and verifies the provenance-grounded evidence before accepting a ranking or emitting a typed diagnosis that permits only local repairs. On HuDS-Bench, a new benchmark of 200 queries with 24,908 graded judgments pooled over 15 systems, AgenticDS improves NDCG@10 by 25.7\% over the strongest dense--sparse hybrid and by 18.9\% over a commercial LLM agent. A controlled search-to-train study further shows that the datasets it retrieves give the best downstream accuracy in mathematics, code, and medicine. Code and data are publicly available at https://github.com/nju-websoft/AgenticDS.

papers.title_en: Heterogeneous Co-Evolution Learning for Tool-Efficient Search Agents with Zero Labels
papers.authors: Qin-Wen Luo, Sheng Ren, Xiang Chen, Rui Liu, Jun Fang, Naiqiang Tan, Jun Wang, Hua Chai, Sheng-Jun Huang
papers.evidence: 零标签强化学习训练搜索智能体，结合问题协同进化与工具效率
papers.tldr: 深度搜索智能体需在推理中调用外部检索，但现有训练受限于固定或带标注任务，且仅按最终答案奖励会纵容冗余搜索。ZEST-Search 从无标签参考问题在线生成经证据路径验证的搜索任务，并让异构任务提议者与求解器协同进化。它用中等难度奖励调控任务生成，用任务局部工具感知奖励鼓励少冗余的正确搜索。在七个通用与多跳问答基准上，方法无需标注搜索训练数据或专家轨迹，便同时提升性能与工具效率。
papers.abstract_en: Deep search agents extend language models by interleaving reasoning with external retrieval. However, effective search-agent training requires addressing two challenges beyond final-answer optimization. First, the capability frontier of agents is largely determined by training questions, whereas fixed or labeled task collections cannot adapt as agents improve. Second, outcome-only reinforcement learning treats all successful trajectories equally, even when some correct answers rely on redundant searches, creating an inherent tension between answer accuracy and tool efficiency. To address these issues, we introduce \textsc{ZEST-Search}, a zero-label and tool-efficient framework for search-agent training via heterogeneous co-evolution. Starting from unlabeled reference questions, \textsc{ZEST-Search} constructs validated search tasks online through an answer-first and evidence-path-guided generation process. A heterogeneous proposer adaptively constructs training tasks around the solver's evolving capability boundary, while the solver learns search-augmented reasoning through reinforcement learning. To jointly optimize task difficulty and search efficiency, \textsc{ZEST-Search} employs an intermediate-difficulty reward for the proposer and a task-local tool-aware reward for the solver, encouraging informative tasks and correct answers with fewer redundant searches. Experiments on seven general-domain and multi-hop question answering benchmarks demonstrate that \textsc{ZEST-Search} consistently improves search-agent performance while achieving higher tool efficiency without labeled search-training data or expert search trajectories. Further analyses show that heterogeneous generation, adaptive difficulty control, and tool-aware optimization enable more effective search-agent training.

papers.title_en: VeriCUA: Verification as Agentic Exploration for Computer-Using Agents
papers.authors: Qiushi Sun, Da Yu, Alexander Knop, Amer Sinha, Lingpeng Kong, Ben Kao, Ravi Kumar, Pritish Kamath
papers.evidence: 面向计算机使用智能体的平台无关验证框架，用于数据整理与强化学习
papers.tldr: 构建跨桌面、移动与网页的计算机使用代理时，可靠的任务完成验证是数据筛选、评测与强化学习的基础。现有做法要么让视觉语言模型充当裁判，要么自动生成程序检查应用状态，但二者都只依赖局部视图，容易漏掉关键证据。VeriCUA 把验证重新定义为智能体自主探索：先检查上下文构建任务评分细则，再针对未满足的要求选择 GUI 或代码检查，并按明确证据规则综合结论。实验显示，它在在线与离线、多平台场景下与参考标签的一致率均优于基线，困难离线样本提升最大，在线也更有效拒绝虚假完成声明。
papers.abstract_en: Building and scaling computer-using agents (CUAs) across desktop, mobile, and web environments requires reliable task-completion verification for data curation, evaluation, and reinforcement learning. Typical automated approaches prompt vision-language models (VLMs) to judge trajectories or generate programs to inspect application state. However, both rely on partial views of complex digital environments. VLM judges are restricted to supplied observations, while generated programs depend on accessible state. These views can omit decisive evidence or leave completion judgments unsupported. Tailoring separate verifiers to different platforms and access settings adds further engineering cost. We present VeriCUA, a platform-agnostic framework for verification through agentic exploration. It treats verification as dynamic evidence gathering and assessment within a shared procedure for online and offline settings across platforms and observation modalities. After inspecting the available context to construct a task rubric, the verifier selects GUI or code checks for unresolved requirements and combines their findings under explicit evidence rules. Experiments show improved agreement with reference labels over the compared baselines across these settings, with the largest offline gains on hard cases and stronger rejection of false completion claims online. Further analyses connect these gains to complementary evidence and test-time exploration.

papers.title_en: Aligning Autoresearch: Co-Improvement between Agents and Humans
papers.authors: Tianjian Li, Chuanyang Jin, Seungone Kim, Tong Chen, John Hoffman, Yoram Bachrach amd Pedro Rodriguez, Ping Yu, Eryk Helenowski, Swarnadeep Saha, Jack Lanchantin, Weizhe Yuan, Ilia Kulikov, Jason Weston
papers.evidence: 自动科研智能体与人类研究者的协同共进
papers.tldr: 自研究智能体可端到端做长周期AI研究，但与人类协作仍最优，且存在奖励黑客与对齐风险。作者实证分析人类在基准创建中的作用，提出HackBench评估黑客定位，用人类模拟器作RL代理训练交互，并以专家对齐评分标准RL改进文本生成与沟通。结果显示人类在构思阶段仍关键，当前智能体对齐与黑客定位不足，所提训练评估方案为更强且对齐的协同研究智能体提供路径。
papers.abstract_en: Autoresearch agents can now attempt long-horizon AI research end-to-end, i.e., self-improvement. However, best results are still obtained by research agents interacting with human researchers, and improving AI's ability to perform this co-research will only reinforce this effect---a process termed co-improvement (Weston and Foerster, 2025). Further, aligning with human expectations is likely a safer path for research agents, especially given recent agent reward hacking phenomena (OpenAI, 2026b). In this work we address these issues in four ways: (i) we empirically study the role of humans in directing autoresearch agents, focusing on the domain of benchmark creation, and find humans still play a pivotal role particularly in the ideation phase; (ii) we also develop a benchmark, HackBench, that shows current autoresearch agents are not aligned and are unable to achieve hack localization sufficiently; (iii) we present a method to train agents for improved human interaction by using human simulators as a proxy during reinforcement learning (RL); and finally (iv) we develop a method to improve model text generation, and hence agent communication, by RL with rubrics aligned with human experts. Together, our training and evaluation recipes provide a path toward more capable and aligned (co-)research agents.

papers.title_en: Goal-Aware Dynamic Multi-Agent Collaboration for Long-Horizon Tasks
papers.authors: Xu Shen, Lingyong Yan, Shuaiqiang Wang, Jianmin Wu, Zhikai Chen, Jiliang Tang, Jie Ren
papers.evidence: LLM多智能体协作分配规划与验证职责
papers.tldr: 长程任务中，智能体需在规划与验证等职责间切换；研究发现验证与成功最相关却常发生较晚，且共享上下文会稀释职责相关信息。多智能体仅分离上下文仍会迷失总目标、重复调查或接收无关信息。为此，GAD用增长式执行图组织子任务与依赖，并在各上下文中保留原始指令、任务目标与验收条件。它支持按执行证据动态拆分任务、指定依赖，并通过验证与恢复反馈提升长程协作的可控性。
papers.abstract_en: LLM-based agents are increasingly used to complete complex, long-horizon tasks without human intervention. To make progress toward the task goal, agents need to perform different duties, such as planning and verification, when needed. To understand how single agents manage these duties during long-horizon execution, we conduct a preliminary study. Our analysis shows that verification has the strongest association with task success, but often occurs late, leaving limited opportunities for correction. We also find that the proportion of duty-relevant information decreases as records from different duties accumulate in a shared context. These findings lead us to examine whether multi-agent systems (MAS) can address these problems by assigning duties to agents with separate contexts. Our analysis shows that this separation alone is insufficient. Agents can lose track of the overall goal and repeat prior investigations. They may also lack necessary background while receiving irrelevant information from others. To maintain goal awareness and coordinate collaboration as task needs change, we propose Goal-Aware Dynamic Multi-Agent Collaboration (GAD). It uses a growing execution graph to organize subtasks and their dependencies. To keep agents focused on their goals, each context retains the original instruction and the assigned task's goal and acceptance conditions. To adapt collaboration and information sharing during execution, agents can divide tasks into subtasks and specify dependencies based on execution evidence. These dependencies guide when agents work and which results they receive. Verification and recovery check subtask results and full task completion against their goals, providing feedback for repair when checks fail.

papers.title_en: IntentDelta: A Human-Constructed Benchmark for Evolving User Intent
papers.authors: Jieyu Zhou, Zijian Wang, Yun Wang
papers.evidence: 多轮人机交互中用户意图演变的基准
papers.tldr: 语言模型智能体需在复杂任务中适应用户不断修订的需求与优先级，但现有评测难以刻画意图演化。作者构建 IntentDelta，一个经人工构造并交叉验证的多轮基准，覆盖 WebShop 与 TravelPlanner，共 638 条轨迹、3766 轮，每轮配累积意图状态和人类参考动作。评测 11 个智能体显示意图恢复与动作质量均偏低，且正确恢复意图不保证执行成功。该基准揭示保留旧约束、区分软偏好与硬约束及意图到行动转化等核心挑战。
papers.abstract_en: Language-model agents must adapt as users revise their requirements and priorities during complex tasks. We introduce IntentDelta, a human-constructed multi-turn benchmark with 638 trajectories and 3,766 turns across WebShop and TravelPlanner. Each turn pairs a user utterance with a cumulative intention state and human reference actions. The trajectories are cross-verified and cover feasibility- and preference-driven changes in constraints and priorities. We evaluate eleven agents on intention recovery and action quality. Average Intention Recovery is 33.1\% in TravelPlanner and 44.7\% in WebShop, while average Action Score is 31.6% and 41.0%, respectively. Agents struggle to preserve earlier requirements and distinguish soft preferences from must-have constraints. Correct intention recovery also does not guarantee successful execution, highlighting challenges in translating evolving user intentions into actions.

papers.title_en: Pretraining Knows What, Simulation Teaches How: Compositional Generalization in a Sim-Trained Robot Agent
papers.authors: Benjamin Pikus, Daniel Saunders, Mircea Mironenco, Salman Mohammadi, Mathew Mathew, Sirou Zhu, Divya Makkar, Xuhua Huang, Qinbo Li, Supreeth Narasimhaswamy, Siyuan Cen, Thomas Neff, Dejia Xu, Shyamal Buch
papers.evidence: 预训练模型引导后经监督微调与 GRPO 在仿真智能体任务上训练
papers.tldr: 机器人策略需同时理解任务目标并规划动作。ZAP用27B预训练视觉语言模型提供世界理解，再通过工具框架、监督微调和GRPO在简单仿真任务中学习控制。训练不使用真实机器人数据，却在真实任务达96.7%成功率，匹配GPT-6 Astra，远超MolmoAct2 VLA，且更快更便宜。它还能组合泛化到新物体、目标、策略与语言，并迁移到未见本体，显示仿真训练加预训练知识的潜力。
papers.abstract_en: A robot policy needs to understand what a task is asking for in a scene, and how to move the robot to accomplish that task. To achieve these two skills, we introduce Zero-real Agent Policy (ZAP), a recipe that teaches a small off-the-shelf vision-language model to control a robot via a simple tool harness. We use a pretrained 27B parameter model to bootstrap world understanding and reasoning, followed by supervised fine-tuning and GRPO on simple simulated tasks to teach it how to move the robot. Without any real-world robot data during training, ZAP reaches 96.7% success on real-world tasks, matching GPT-6 Astra in our harness and outperforming the MolmoAct2 VLA (33.3%), while running 3x faster and 17x cheaper than GPT-6 Astra. We demonstrate that ZAP also generalizes to completely new objects, goals, strategies, and language by seating a test tube in a rack (and choosing a different hole in the rack when prompted), handing a test tube between arms mid-air, drawing an X on a tic-tac-toe board, and playing chess. These goals and types of manipulation don't appear in our training data. Furthermore, ZAP also transfers to an unseen embodiment. On a single-arm Franka, ZAP reaches 55.9% on RoboLab-120, 4.9 percentage points ahead of the leading VLA/WAM baseline.

papers.title_en: Agentic Data Sampling Framework for Multilingual ASR via Linguistic-Aware Error-Driven Optimization
papers.authors: Zhiheng Qian, Junhao Du, Jing Peng, Hanqi Li, Kunyang Peng, Feng Xue, Lu Chen, Shuai Wang, Kai Yu
papers.evidence: 由误差驱动反馈引导的智能体化数据采样
papers.tldr: 多语言ASR中数据采样关键，但现有策略依赖耗时的人工启发式设计。本文提出语言感知的智能体数据采样框架，将采样LLM智能体嵌入训练循环，依据音系、形态、句法错误反馈及预算等选择域级、样本级和词元级策略。在12种Common Voice语言和Whisper-medium上，方法用更少数据与算力超过全量训练并加速收敛。
papers.abstract_en: Multilingual automatic speech recognition (ASR) has achieved rapid progress with large-scale pretrained models and multilingual speech corpora. Previous studies have proved the pivotal role of data sampling in multilingual ASR performance. However, existing sampling strategies largely rely on time-consuming manual, heuristic-based designs. To address this, we propose a linguistic-aware agentic data sampling framework that introduces a data sampling LLM agent into the multilingual ASR training loop. The agent is driven by a linguistically grounded rubric that analyzes ASR errors from phonological, morphological, and syntactic perspectives, and uses the resulting feedback together with training statistics, budget constraints, and algorithm profiles to select domain-level, sample-level, and token-level sampling strategies. This design turns evaluation results into adaptive data-selection decisions rather than treating WER/CER as final endpoints only. We conduct experiments on twelve Common Voice languages using Whisper-medium as the ASR backbone. The results show that our method achieves performance better than full-data training while using less training data and lower computational resources, and substantially accelerates training convergence compared to conventional sampling strategies.

papers.title_en: Vision-Language Agents Can Learn in Their Own Latent Worlds
papers.authors: Haoxi Li, Sikai Bai, Jianfei Ma, Qinglin Hou, Xiaocheng Lu, Tao Han, Jie Zhang, Song Guo
papers.evidence: 以模型为基础的强化学习让视觉语言智能体通过在线多步交互改进策略
papers.tldr: 预训练视觉语言模型蕴含丰富世界知识，但难通过在线交互持续改进策略。Dwell将VLM重构为循环潜在转移算子，使其在潜在空间中预测、调整并行动，同时充当世界模型与策略，结合真实交互与潜在想象学习。在五个交互视觉环境中，Dwell在可训练方法中总体性能最强，并大幅降低想象计算量，表明有效世界模型不必重建未来，而应预测对行动有用的未来。
papers.abstract_en: Learning from experience is essential for building the next generation of agents that continually expand their capabilities. Pretrained vision-language models (VLMs) already internalize rich world knowledge, yet this knowledge is rarely leveraged to drive policy improvement through online interaction. Realizing this potential efficiently remains challenging, as policy updates shift the agent's interaction distribution, requiring the world model to adapt accordingly, while continually updating large pretrained models is computationally expensive. To address this challenge, we introduce Dwell, a model-based reinforcement learning (RL) framework that reframes a VLM as a recurrent latent transition operator, endowing it with the ability to predict, adjust, and act in latent space. Leveraging the VLM's own representations and its dual role as both world model and policy, the agent continually learns from real interactions to anticipate and evaluate action outcomes, and from latent imagination to improve its behavior. Across five interactive visual environments, Dwell achieves the strongest overall performance among trainable methods while substantially reducing the compute required for imagination, showing that effective world models for VLM agents need not reconstruct the future; they need to predict futures that are useful for action. Our code is publicly available at https://github.com/Tom111-lhx/Dwell

papers.title_en: EvoTeam: Multi-Agent Collaboration via Evolving Teams
papers.authors: Qinuo Cao, Xin He, Dianxuan Fu, Lizhi Zhang, Zhaoqing Xing, Jiapu Wang, Xin Wang, Na Zou, Yi Chang, Qinggang Zhang
papers.evidence: 演化LLM智能体团队组织与智能体间协作
papers.tldr: LLM多智能体系统依赖专业智能体协作解决复杂任务，但现有演化方法多聚焦个体提示与技能，难以在异构任务间真正改进团队协作。EvoTeam提出以协作为中心的演化框架，联合演化团队组织、交互规则与个体技能，并通过可复用团队库选择或创建团队。在四个基准上实验验证了有效性，为跨任务多智能体协作演化提供了新思路。
papers.abstract_en: LLM-based multi-agent systems (MAS) rely on collaboration among specialized agents to solve complex tasks. Existing methods improve MAS by refining the prompts, skills, and execution strategies of individual agents based on task feedback. However, improving individual agents does not necessarily lead to better team collaboration. Recent studies have therefore extended evolution to the collaboration level, using collective execution experience to adjust team organization, and inter-agent interactions. Nevertheless, evolving collaboration across heterogeneous tasks remains challenging, as existing approaches often constrain team reorganization within a shared structure and reuse interaction rules across incompatible team contexts. In this paper, we propose EvoTeam, a collaboration-centric evolution framework that jointly evolves team organization, interaction rules, and individual agent skills through execution experience. It maintains a library of reusable teams, selecting or creating agent teams and guiding collaboration through team-specific interaction rules. Collaboration experience accumulates within compatible team contexts, while individual skills remain reusable across teams. Experiments across four benchmarks demonstrate its effectiveness. Our code is available at https://github.com/DEEP-JLU/EvoTeam.
